papers.title: Synthetic Study Alpha: CO2 photoreduction over Cu-doped catalysts

paragraphs.text: We report a synthetic benchmark study on CO2 photoreduction using Cu-doped TiO2 samples and a fixed-bed reactor at 25 °C. The measured CO yield of 45 umol g-1 h-1 is higher than the undoped reference under the same condition.
Cu-doped TiO2 samples were prepared by impregnation. Phase identification was carried out using in situ XRD, and electronic structure was examined using DFT calculations.
Under visible light at 25 °C, the Cu-doped catalyst shows a CO selectivity of 92% and outperforms the undoped catalyst, which reaches only 61% selectivity.
These results indicate that Cu doping stabilizes the active site. However, the long-term stability remains unreported in this synthetic text.
We conclude that Cu-doped TiO2 is more active than the undoped reference at 25 °C, while the origin of the selectivity gap is not resolved here.

papers.title: Synthetic Study Beta: CO2 photoreduction over N-doped catalysts

paragraphs.text: This synthetic study examines N-doped TiO2 samples for CO2 photoreduction in a slurry reactor at 15 °C. The measured CO yield of 30 umol g-1 h-1 is lower than reported values for Cu-doped systems.
N-doped TiO2 samples were obtained by annealing under ammonia. Product analysis was performed using gas chromatography, and the electronic structure was examined using DFT calculations.
At 15 °C the N-doped catalyst reaches a CO selectivity of 88%, and it outperforms the undoped reference under the same condition.
Li Wei et al. reported a selectivity of 92% for Cu-doped catalysts, which is consistent with our observation that doping suppresses H2 evolution.
These results show that N-doped TiO2 is active at 15 °C, but a direct comparison with the Cu-doped system tested at 25 °C cannot be made from these data alone.
